newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA RUBBER FUTURES SEEN FALLING AS LONGS SELL.
newsitem.headline: CHINA RUBBER FUTURES SEEN FALLING AS LONGS SELL.

text.p: Rubber futures on the China Commodity Futures Exchange will fall further in the short term because long position holders are unwilling to take physical delivery and are selling futures in volume, traders said on Tuesday.

Price moves, however, would be limited by crackdown measures recently introduced by the exchange to cool a ferocious battle between longs and shorts in the key August 1997 contract, analysts and traders said.

The battle led to huge fluctuations in the price of the August contract, and led the exchange to increase margin requirements, dramatically cut limit-up and limit-down levels, close down two warehouses and suspend trading for a day while the board met to discuss market risk.
Holders of big positions in the exchange's August contract had tried to force prices up to squeeze those traders who sold forward, traders said.
This led to huge price swings as the longs, or holders of physical rubber, and the shorts, holders of forward contracts, battled to dominate the August contract and dictate prices.

Trading was suspended last Wednesday for a meeting on market risk, which led to new regulations limiting price movements in the August 1997 contract to within 40 yuan per day from last Friday in an effort to bring some control to the market.
The former daily limit-up and limit-down levels for the contract were 400 yuan, traders said.
The exchange also said it would lift the margin requirement of the contract to 80 percent from Wednesday, August 13, from the usual 6.5 percent.
The clampdown measures made it difficult for long position holders to offset their positions and forced them to take delivery of physical rubber, traders said.
The volume of physical rubber that longs were expected to take was a key factor in deciding price movements of the September contract, they said.
The longs were now building short positions in the September contract as a way of offsetting the physical deliveries they must take from the maturing August contract.
Delivery in the August contract begins on August 18.

"The price of the September contract will fall further and it is hard to see where support will be as we cannot know how much physical rubber the longs may take," said one trader with a futures brokerage based in southern Hainan province.
"Longs have been seen building short positions in the September contract, and that led to solid falls in the contract," he said.
The price of the September contract ended Monday down 226 yuan at 8,275 yuan per tonne after suffering more than 500 yuan in losses over the past four trading days.
This compared with a spot price of around 11,000 yuan per tonne, traders said.
The exchange was still trying to make longs and shorts negotiate the August contract, but no agreements had been reached, they said.
Traders said they expected the exchange to use part of its risk control fund to help absorb some physical rubber.
Around 150,000 tonnes of physical rubber was now availabe for delivery, traders said.
